findings.proposed: Leave the wording as-is for this migration; raise separately whether `tim start <service>` should be config-driven.
findings.why: SILENT ASSUMPTION, not a string. The documented command surface hard-codes exactly three startable services (frontend / backend / admin) — which today resolve to the animals sub-repos. That is fine under R2 while animals is the only commodity line, but once the workspace is generic a second line would need `tim start` to read a service list from config rather than from a fixed three-way subcommand set. The hard-coding itself lives in `tim/src/commands/` (out of this scope). Human must rule: leave as an animals-shaped convenience, or make it config-driven. Same question applies to `tim docker bounce-backend` (line 55).
